cite: KB-M2K-M3K-PRESETS: 'it is not possible to dump your M2000 presets into the M3000', 'They are simply not inter-compatible.'

tcStatement.consequence: No pair below is 'documented-same': no TC document states that an M2000 algorithm and an M3000 algorithm are the same. Any transfer is a re-creation by parameter mapping, never a preset load.

contradictions.b: KB-M2K-VSS3 (M2000 reverbs from the M5000) + M3K-EN p.46 (Rev 3 from the M5000) + TC-REVCMP (Rev3 in both)
contradictions.handling: compatible readings: the reverb sets differ overall, a shared M5000 ancestry of Rev 3 is not excluded; identity unproven (FAMILY-COMPATIBILITY §7)

contradictions.b: M3K-EN p.47: 'up to 1350ms', otherwise the same sentence
contradictions.handling: documented difference (FAMILY-COMPATIBILITY X9): not the same algorithm as documented

statusSemantics.confirmed: both units print the range and unit of this parameter, same label and physical quantity; the conversion is exact (M2000 side 'confirmed' in M2000-PARAMETERS.json and M3000 side 'confirmed' in DISPLAY-MAP.json).
statusSemantics.hypothesis: the pairing is plausible (same label or meaning) but at least one side's range/unit/order is not printed; conversion 'none' means no value law can be derived and an editor must not transfer the value silently.
statusSemantics.none: no counterpart row in that M3000 algorithm (m3000Id null).

relationSemantics.documented-same: a TC document states the two algorithms are the same (none found).
relationSemantics.documented-derived: TC documents state a derivation: one from the other, or both from a common ancestor (here: M2000 reverbs and M3000 Rev 3 both 'from the M5000'); identity is not stated.
relationSemantics.same-name-only: the algorithm (or variant) names coincide, often with near-identical manual wording, without any statement of identity or derivation.
relationSemantics.similar-function: different names, comparable function and partially overlapping parameter names.

pairs.note: 'documented-derived' = common M5000 ancestry, the strongest relation found: TC support says the M2000 reverbs come from the M5000 (KB-M2K-VSS3) and the M3000 manual says Rev 3 comes from the M5000 (M3K-EN p.46); only TC's comparison sheet names 'Rev3' for the M2000, and the M2000 manual does not say which of its reverb types (if any) is Rev 3. No source states identity, and TC support says the M3000 uses other reverb algorithms and that presets are not compatible (X3). Contradiction X1 (FAMILY-COMPATIBILITY §7), both readings kept: TC-REVCMP gives the M3000 'VSS3, Rev2, Rev3' while the M3000's own documents (M3K-EN p.5, M3K-SYX p.5) list VSS3, VSS Gate, VSS-FP, VSS-SR, C.O.R.E. and Rev 3, with no 'Rev 2'; whether the sheet's 'Rev2' designates C.O.R.E. is unknown.

routingMapNote: Both units number six routings 1-6 on their ROUTING LCD (M2K-EN p.16; M3K-EN p.18 via DISPLAY-MAP MIDI_ROUTING). Five names match; M2000 STEREO and M3000 LINKED both copy Engine 1 into Engine 2 (M2K-EN p.16; M3000 dossier §12). Index = LCD number - 1 is an inference on both sides, hence 'hypothesis'. The M2000 sends ROUTING on CC 35 (M2K-CC), the M3000 on CC 44 (M3K-SYX p.4).
